newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: ECNZ investigates possible Wellington wind farm.
newsitem.headline: ECNZ investigates possible Wellington wind farm.

text.p: Electricity Corporation of New Zealand (ECNZ) said on Friday it was beginning a new series of investigations into a possible wind farm at Makara, near Wellington, with potential for over 30 Megawatts.
After evaluating a number of Wellington sites, ECNZ had bought the former Telecom Makara Farm property, also known as Quartz Hill.

"Although our investigation is at very early stages the Makara site is ideal for between 40 and 80 turbines, depending on the chosen size. This could produce up to 170 GWh (Gigawatt hours) of electricity each year which would be sufficient to supply eight percent of the electricity needs of Wellington, Porirua and the Hutt Valley," said ECNZ's general manager of strategic development, John Boshier.
Boshier said the site, which is not visible from most of Wellington, could be easily linked into the regional electricity network.

He said ECNZ's experimental site in Brooklyn had proved its worth as a testing-ground for the performance of wind turbines under local weather conditions. Wellington's weather made the city an ideal location for a wind farm.
